sets.name: SVE first-word-frequency model
sets.basis: Both apply the Semiotic Virality Engine's first-word-frequency model to a specific coined term's propagation.

evidence.phrase: The SVE's first-word-frequency model predicts this
a two-word ghost phrase with a high-frequency first word will propagate more slowly

observations: PRED-38.G3 and PRED-950.G11 (TP24.2) appear to run the SVE first-word-frequency model in opposite directions: 38.G3 says high-frequency first words ('predatory') propagate faster than neologistic ones, while 950.G11 says a high-frequency first word ('ghost') will propagate more slowly than a low-frequency one. Deposit #950 holds both at lines 8450 and 8458; the comparison classes differ (neologistic vs low-frequency first word). Recorded as an apparent contradiction, not resolved.

PRED-880.G1 (TP24.2, high bystanding scores as the common false-positive) belongs with the same set PRED-825.G1 / PRED-833.G1 (TP24.1) on compositional bystanding; it names the reading error the bystanding pattern produces, and was left unlinked as a distinct claim.

PRED-1550.G3 ('low-density true entities are dissolved by high-density false ones', TP24.2) belongs with PRED-147.G1 (substitution by the nearest high-density modal cluster) and PRED-172.A2 (undefended low-density coined terms merge); PRED-1633.G1 ('Vulnerability is nomination, not volume'; low mass varies either way) stands in apparent tension with a density-only reading of these. Not linked as same or states because 1550.G3 grounds survival in density per address space and 147.G1 in institutional prior position.

PRED-305.G1 (low-frequency content flushed first; 'The rare disappears. The common persists.') and PRED-907.G1 (H1 long-tail fragility under recursive defiguration) state a near thesis under different mechanisms; left separate.

PRED-1079.E4 (registered 2026-07-14) narrates a term surviving in Oakland in 2027 and calls it confirmed; the deposit is dated before the event it reports, which reads as the Grundrisse's speculative-future register rather than a wrong date.

PRED-1450.B3 and PRED-1450.H3 (same deposit) are the forecast and historical halves of one argument (saves came through independent channels; channel independence is eroding); left separate as distinct claims.
